The '''2017–18 Ekstraklasa''' (also known as '''Lotto Ekstraklasa''' due to its [[Sponsor (commercial)|sponsorship]] by Totalizator Sportowy, Polish [[lottery]])<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.ekstraklasa.org/lotto-partnerem-tytularnym-ekstraklasy |title=LOTTO Partnerem Tytularnym Ekstraklasy |website=www.ekstraklasa.org |date=14 July 2016 |access-date=15 July 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160718034522/http://www.ekstraklasa.org/lotto-partnerem-tytularnym-ekstraklasy |archive-date=2016-07-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref> was the 92nd season of [[List of Polish football champions|the Polish Football Championship]], the 84th season of [[Sports league|the highest tier domestic division]] in the [[Polish football league system]] since its establishment in [[1927 Ekstraklasa|1927]] and the 10th season of the [[Ekstraklasa]] under its current title. The league was operated by the Ekstraklasa [[S.A. (corporation)|SA]].

The season started on 14 July 2017 and concluded on 20 May 2018.<ref name="Terminarz">{{cite web |url=http://www.90minut.pl/news/278/news2782240-Terminarz-Ekstraklasy-2017-18.html |title=Terminarz Ekstraklasy 2017/18 |publisher = 90minut.pl |date=8 June 2017 |access-date=9 June 2017}}</ref> It is the first Ekstraklasa season to use [[Video assistant referee|VAR]]. After the 21st matchday the league went on a winter break between 18 December 2017 and 9 February 2018. The regular season was played as a [[round-robin tournament]]. A total of 16 teams participated, 14 of which competed in the league during the 2016–17 season, while the remaining two were promoted from the [[2016–17 I liga|I liga]] after the 2016–17 season. The fixtures were announced on 8 June 2017.<ref name="Terminarz"/>

Each team played a total of 30 matches, half at home and half away. After the 30th round (in the beginning of April 2018), the league split into two groups: ''championship round'' (top eight teams) and ''relegation round'' (bottom eight teams). Each team played 7 more games (teams ranked 1-4 and 9-12 played four times at home). So, finally each team played a total of 37 matches. The team at the top of the Championship round wins the league title. The two teams at the bottom of the Relegation round are demoted to [[I liga]] for the 2018–19 season. This was the fifth season to take place since the new playoff structure has been introduced.

The defending champions were [[Legia Warsaw]], who won their 12th Polish title [[2016–17 Ekstraklasa|the previous season]].

Legia successfully defended their title, sealing the league trophy for a 13th time in dramatic circumstances as their deciding game against [[Lech Poznań|Lech Poznan]] was abandoned due to flares and pitch invasions by Lech fans (after Legia went 2-0 ahead).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44193876|title=Legia Warsaw win Polish Championship after Lech Poznan game abandoned|date=2018-05-21|work=BBC Sport|access-date=2018-05-21|language=en-GB}}</ref> Legia were awarded the tie 3-0 and three points secured 1st place.

==Teams==
Sixteen teams will compete in the league – the top fourteen teams from the previous season, as well as two teams promoted from the [[2016–17 I liga|I liga]]. [[Sandecja Nowy Sącz]] were promoted to the Ekstraklasa for the first time.<ref>{{cite web | title = Historyczny awans Sandecji do ekstraklasy | publisher = rp.pl | date = 17 May 2017 | url = http://www.rp.pl/Pilka-nozna/170519024-Historyczny-awans-Sandecji-do-ekstraklasy.html | access-date = 18 May 2017 }}</ref> [[Górnik Zabrze]] returned to [[Ekstraklasa]] after a one-year absence.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.90minut.pl/news/278/news2781097-Gornik-w-Lotto-Ekstraklasie.html |title=Górnik w Lotto Ekstraklasie |publisher=90minut |date=4 June 2017 |access-date=4 June 2017}}</ref>
